info.title: Thulu API
info.description: The HTTP API of Thulu, a task board where an agent (Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode) works each stage and a person decides what merges.

responses.unknown_stream: Unknown stream, or owned by another caller

task.body: Markdown description. Populated by {route} only — the list endpoints return it empty so a board poll does not carry every description.

test_case.key: TC-<n> unless given; unique per task. {param} in a path accepts it or the id
test_case.status: pending, pass, fail, blocked or skipped

test_case_run.report_id: The evidence report in the Reports tab
test_case_run.comment_id: Where runs recorded before reports existed kept their report

webhook.secret: Signing secret; returned only on creation and rotation
webhook.legacy_signing: Signed with HMAC keyed by hex(sha256(secret)) until the secret is rotated

audit_chain_report.checked: Rows whose hash was recomputed and matched
audit_chain_report.legacy: Rows written before the chain existed
audit_chain_report.broken_at: Id of the first row that failed
audit_chain_report.head: Hash of the newest row; record it outside the database
audit_chain_report.cause: Why that row failed, without its id
audit_chain_report.broken_created_at: When the failed row was written

token_optimizer.reason: why the level is lower than configured: no_worker (the agent names no complete worker, its engine has no usable default profile, or a cli worker for an agent on another engine than claude-code, whose image has no claude) or engine_without_hooks (enforce on an agent whose engine runs no hooks); empty otherwise
token_optimizer.via: how the run reaches the worker: api (the daemon calls the provider with the default profile's key, which never reaches the pod) or cli (the run's own pod runs the Claude Code CLI with the default profile's subscription token); empty when there is no usable worker
token_optimizer.provider: the provider of the engine's default LLM profile
token_optimizer.engine: the worker's engine: claude-code, codex or opencode
token_optimizer.model: the worker's model, from the agent's definition
token_optimizer.available: whether the engine's default LLM profile can back a worker
token_optimizer.worker_reason: why the worker is not available: no_default_profile or unsupported_credential; empty otherwise
token_optimizer.profile_name: the name of the engine's default LLM profile

workspace_run_limit.about: The wall-clock limit on one agent run in this workspace, in minutes
workspace_run_limit.value: the workspace's own choice; null when it chose none
workspace_run_limit.default: the install's limit, what a workspace without a value gets; 0 = no limit
workspace_run_limit.ceiling: the most a workspace may choose
workspace_run_limit.effective: what the workspace's runs get: min(value, ceiling), or the default
workspace_run_limit.body: whole minutes from 1 to the ceiling, or null to go back to the install default

params.board: Filter by board (the task's workflow). Preferred over stage: a stage id can belong to several boards.
params.stage: Filter by stage (e.g. backlog, in_progress, done)
params.limit: Page size. Omit for the whole list. Capped at 500.
params.cursor: Opaque token from a previous response's X-Next-Cursor header. Absence of that header means the last page was reached.

list_attachments.summary: List every attachment on the task

upload_attachment.description: Two request shapes on one route: multipart/form-data with the file in the `file` part, or application/json with the bytes in `content_base64`. Both accept `comment_id` (bind the file to a comment on this task). The author comes from the credential. 50MB per file.

delete_attachment.summary: Delete an attachment and its file

list_sections.summary: Parsed structured sections of the task body

set_section.summary: Create or replace one body section

list_pull_requests.summary: Read the state, CI and review of the task's pull requests
list_pull_requests.description: Answers {pull_requests: [...]}, one row per project with a pull request: project_id, project_name, url, number, title, state (open, draft, merged, closed), head, base, ci {source (checks or actions), total, passed, failed, running, state (none, running, passed, failed)}, review (none, pending, approved, changes_requested), mergeable (ready, blocked, behind, conflicts, unknown), changed_files, additions, deletions, commits, updated_at. A pull request GitHub would not answer for keeps project_id, project_name and url, with error (the catalog key) and error_message instead of the rest. Answers are cached for 30 seconds; GitHub webhooks about a pull request, its reviews or its checks drop them sooner. ci.source is actions when the GitHub App lacks Checks: read: only GitHub Actions jobs are counted then.

list_reports.summary: List the task's reports, oldest first

add_report.summary: File a report in the Reports tab
add_report.description: kind is evidence or agent_index (agent runs only); auditor feedback has its own route. body is markdown, up to 256 KB. instance_id, when given, must be a run of this task. Reports never post a comment, launch or notify anyone.

list_test_cases.summary: List the task's test cases, each with its runs

add_test_cases.summary: Add one test case, or several as {cases: [...]}
add_test_cases.description: Returns the created cases. A case without a key gets TC-<max+1>; a taken key answers 409.

import_test_cases_from_body.summary: Turn the body's Test Cases checklist into cases, skipping titles already present

delete_test_case.summary: Delete a test case and its runs

record_test_case_run.summary: Record a run of a test case
record_test_case_run.description: verdict is required. Every attachment, report and comment id must belong to the task (404 otherwise). The case takes the verdict as its status and counts as covered. Answers {run, test_case}.

list_workspace_test_cases.summary: QA view: test cases across the caller's workspace
list_workspace_test_cases.description: Answers {test_cases: [...], counts: {status: n}, covered_counts: {status: n}}. Each row is a TestCase without runs, plus task_title, task_stage, board_id, last_run and runs_count. Both counts have every status over the whole filtered set, the status filter left out; covered_counts counts only covered cases.

params.q: Matches case key, case title and task title

ask_question.summary: Ask people a question (agent stage runs only)
ask_question.description: Body: task_ask's input {kind, blocking, context, questions: [{header, question, options: [{label, description}], multi_select, allow_other}], default}. Only the task's live stage run may call it, with its own run key. Answers {question, comment_id, instruction}. 409 when the task is not running in the key's stage; 429 past 3 asks per run or 5 open questions per task.

answer_question.description: Body: {answers: [{question_index, selected: [label], other}], note}. A person only; signed with the caller's credential. The answer is posted in the question's thread and handed to the agent: into its live run, or by resuming the stage once every blocking question of that run is answered.

inbox.summary: What waits on a person in the workspace
inbox.description: Answers {questions: [...], approvals: [...]}: agents' open questions and the approvals still holding their stage (pending or with changes requested), each with task_id, task_title and stage, oldest first.

request_approval.description: Body: {label, reason, key}. Opens a pending approval on the task's current stage; moving the task forward out of that stage answers 409 until it is approved or waived. An agent run may call it on its own task.

decide_approval.description: Body: {decision, note}. decision is approved, changes_requested or waived; the last two need a note. A person only. changes_requested does what the stage's on_changes_requested says: resume its agent with the note, send the task back, or stay.

delete_approval.summary: Remove an approval (not one a stage requires: waive that instead)

list_webhook_events.summary: List the events an endpoint can subscribe to

responses.ok: Array of event names; a subscription also accepts * and <prefix>.*

rotate_webhook_secret.summary: Replace the signing secret (returned once) and stop signing with the secret hash

list_webhook_deliveries.summary: List the latest delivery attempts of a webhook

retry_webhook_delivery.summary: Send a logged webhook delivery again

create_automation.summary: Create automation from a YAML spec

validate_automation.summary: Parse a spec without storing it

get_automation_run.summary: One run with its step timeline

verify_audit.summary: Recompute the audit hash chain (operator workspace only)

params.before: Return only messages older than this message id

post_chat_message.summary: Post message (async turn — reply via SSE)

chat_events.summary: SSE stream of chat events (message_added, turn_started/finished/failed, chat_*) — superseded by /events topic "chat"

open_event_stream.summary: Open the multiplexed SSE channel; frames arrive as `msg` events tagged with their topic

params.topics: Comma-separated topics to subscribe on open (chat, logs:<runID>)

responses.ok: text/event-stream; opens with a `hello` event carrying stream_id

subscribe_topics.summary: Add topics to an open stream

unsubscribe_topics.summary: Drop topics from an open stream

upload_project.summary: Create a project from an uploaded folder
upload_project.description: multipart/form-data with two parts in this order: "meta", JSON {name, description, default_board_id, stage_template}, then "archive", the folder as .tar.gz or .zip (200 MB at most). Dependency folders (node_modules, .venv, ...) and files that look like secrets (.env, private keys) are left out and listed in the report. A .git at the top keeps its history; without one the folder is the first commit on main. Answers {project, report}.

reupload_project.summary: Upload a new version of an upload project's folder
reupload_project.description: multipart/form-data with one "archive" part. The folder becomes a commit on the default branch when it differs from what is there; files the upload left out on purpose stay as they were. Answers {project, report}.

params.mode: What to do when the folder came from a commit the default branch has moved past (the zip of a branch from projectArchive names it). Unset: answer 409 with code api.projects.errors.main_moved and ahead. merge: bring those commits along; a clash answers 409 with conflicts. replace: the folder wins.

project_branches.summary: List a project's branches, without task branches

project_archive.summary: Download a branch of the project as a zip

params.branch: Branch to download. The project's default branch when absent.

merge_task.summary: Merge a task's branch into a branch of an uploaded project
merge_task.description: Body {project_id, target}, both optional: the task's only uploaded project and its default branch. Commits what the worktree has, pushes the task branch (rebased onto the default branch), then fast-forwards the target or writes a merge commit. 409 with the conflicting files in conflicts when the branches conflict; nothing is written then. Agent runs cannot call it.

resolve_token_optimizer.summary: What the token optimizer resolves to for an agent

list_token_optimizer_workers.summary: Which engines can answer the token optimizer
list_token_optimizer_workers.description: One entry per registered engine: whether the workspace's default LLM profile for it can back a token optimizer worker, and how a run would reach it. The agent form offers the available ones.

get_workspace_settings.summary: Read the workspace's own settings: its agent run limit and the bounds the install sets

put_workspace_setting.summary: Set or clear one of the workspace's own settings (admin)
